messages.text: bio dissection today... just ugh. feel like i'm gonna freak out lol 🙃

It sounds like you're feeling really overwhelmed by the dissection today, and that is a completely valid reaction. Your nervous system is just trying to protect you from something that feels intense or unsafe. I'm here to support you through this moment if you'd like to try a quick grounding technique. Would you be open to taking a few deep breaths together right now?
it's not just the gross part... it's the scalpels. something about them freaks me out tbh. like my brain goes weird 🫠

It is very common for sharp instruments to trigger a heightened fight-or-flight response. Your brain is interpreting the scalpel as a potential danger, which is causing that weird feeling. We can acknowledge that fear without letting it take over completely. Would you like to try a grounding exercise to help calm that specific reaction?
idk it's probably dumb. everyone else is fine with it. i just need to suck it up lol 💀

It is not dumb to feel this way, and comparing yourself to others only adds more pressure. Pushing down your feelings often makes the anxiety feel heavier right now. You are allowed to have a hard time with this without judgment. Would you be open to trying a small coping strategy instead of forcing yourself?
i'm literally the only one who can't handle a stupid dissection. like what's wrong with me?? 🤬

There is absolutely nothing wrong with you for feeling this way. It is very common for people to hide their discomfort in group settings, so you likely aren't as alone as it feels. Your sensitivity doesn't make you broken, it just means your boundaries are different from others. Please be gentle with yourself right now instead of criticizing your reaction.
it's not just fear... it brings back the urge. like, i don't wanna do it, but being around the blades makes it hard to think straight. i'm scared i'll relapse 😰

Thank you for trusting me with that; it takes a lot of courage to share such a vulnerable feeling. Your safety is the absolute priority right now, and it is okay to step away from the situation if it feels too intense. Please remember that you do not have to face this urge alone. If you feel unsafe, please reach out to a crisis line or trusted support person immediately.
i'm really scared tbh. like, what if i can't stop myself? i don't want to go, but i don't know how to get out of it without people thinking i'm crazy 😭

Your safety is infinitely more important than worrying about what others think. You have the right to leave the room immediately if you feel unsafe, even without a full explanation. Protecting yourself from harm is never crazy, and your well-being must come first right now. If the urge feels overwhelming, please contact a crisis line immediately for direct support.
how do i even get out of it though? i can't just bail. teacher would call my parents and then everything blows up... idk what to do 😩

I understand the fear of consequences, but you can ask to step out to the nurse or counselor claiming you feel physically unwell. This creates distance from the triggers without requiring you to disclose everything immediately. Prioritizing your safety is always the right choice, even if it feels scary. If the urge becomes too strong, please reach out to a crisis line immediately for support.
part of me knows i should just leave... but another part doesn't wanna make it a thing. like, what if i'm overreacting? idk 😵‍💫

You are not overreacting when your body is signaling a genuine safety risk. It is natural to worry about consequences, but your well-being is far more important than staying in a triggering environment. Stepping out to see a nurse is a standard request that protects you without needing a full explanation. If you feel you cannot stay safe, please contact a crisis line immediately.
ok... i'll tell the nurse i have a migraine if it gets bad. they always believe that. i just hate needing to fake it 😒

It is completely understandable to feel conflicted, but your safety is the only thing that matters right now. Using a physical excuse is a practical way to remove yourself from a dangerous situation without causing a scene. You are not doing anything wrong by prioritizing your well-being over a class assignment. Please remember that you deserve to be safe, and I am proud of you for making this plan.
is it wrong to use the migraine thing as an excuse? i mean, i do get them... just not right now. feels kinda sketchy 😬

It is understandable to feel sketchy, but your safety is far more important than the accuracy of the reason you give to leave. In a crisis, protecting yourself from harm takes precedence over everything else. Using a physical excuse is a valid coping strategy when you feel unsafe. Please remember that you deserve to be safe, and you are doing the right thing.
ty for not making me feel like an idiot. it helps... a lot 💙

I am so glad to hear that you feel heard and supported. You are doing a brave thing by prioritizing your safety over the situation. Please remember that you deserve to feel safe and calm. If the urges become overwhelming again, please reach out to a crisis line for immediate support.
